subject: economics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: 4.5-4.6 Exchange rates and balance of payments

questions.q: Free international trade allows countries to:
options: Specialise and gain from exchange, increasing total output
questions.explain: Specialisation according to advantage and trade raises global efficiency and consumption.

questions.q: A tax on imported goods is a:
questions.explain: A tariff raises the price of imports; a quota limits their quantity.

questions.q: A physical limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported is a:
questions.explain: Quotas restrict import quantities, protecting domestic producers.

questions.q: A tariff on imports typically results in:
options: Higher domestic prices and reduced imports
questions.explain: Tariffs raise import prices, reducing the quantity imported and often raising domestic production.

questions.q: A common argument FOR trade protection is:
questions.explain: Protection is defended to let new industries grow, to protect jobs, or on strategic grounds; critics cite inefficiency.

questions.q: A key argument AGAINST protectionism is that it:
options: Raises prices and reduces efficiency and choice for consumers
questions.explain: Protection can cause higher prices, inefficiency, retaliation and welfare loss.

questions.q: A trading bloc in which members trade freely but keep their own external tariffs is a:
questions.explain: A customs union adds a common external tariff; a monetary union shares a currency.

questions.q: A floating exchange rate is determined by:
options: The demand for and supply of the currency
questions.explain: In a floating system, the market sets the exchange rate.

questions.q: A depreciation of a country's currency (floating system) makes its exports:
questions.explain: A weaker currency lowers export prices abroad and raises import prices at home.

questions.q: An appreciation of the domestic currency would tend to:
options: Lower import prices' effect on demand for exports
questions.explain: A stronger currency makes exports dearer abroad and imports cheaper, worsening the trade balance.

questions.q: The current account of the balance of payments records mainly:
options: Trade in goods and services (and income flows)
questions.explain: The current account covers trade in goods and services, primary income and current transfers.

questions.q: A country that imports more goods and services than it exports has a:
questions.explain: Imports exceeding exports contribute to a current account deficit.

questions.q: Economic development is a broader concept than growth because it includes:
options: Improvements in living standards, health, education and welfare
questions.explain: Development considers wellbeing and quality of life, not just output.

questions.q: The Human Development Index (HDI) combines income with:
questions.explain: HDI is a composite measure of income, health and education.

questions.q: Sustainable development is development that:
options: Meets present needs without compromising future generations
questions.explain: It balances economic, social and environmental goals over time.

questions.q: A common barrier to economic development is:
options: Poor infrastructure and low levels of human capital
questions.explain: Weak infrastructure, health, education and institutions constrain development.

questions.q: Investment in education and healthcare promotes development by:
questions.explain: Better-educated, healthier workers are more productive, supporting long-term development.

questions.q: A subsidy given to domestic producers competing with imports:
options: Lowers their costs and can reduce imports
Is the same as a tariff
questions.explain: Production subsidies make domestic goods more competitive against imports, though they have an opportunity cost.

questions.q: In a fixed exchange rate system, the central bank maintains the rate by:
options: Buying and selling its currency (using reserves) and adjusting interest rates
questions.explain: Authorities intervene to keep the currency at the target value.

questions.q: A strategy to promote development through producing goods domestically that were previously imported is:
questions.explain: Import substitution builds domestic industry behind protection; export-led growth instead targets world markets.

questions.q: Trade allows a country to consume:
options: Beyond its own production possibilities curve
questions.explain: Gains from specialisation and trade let a country consume combinations outside its own PPC.

questions.q: Foreign direct investment (FDI) refers to:
options: Investment by multinationals in a country's productive assets
questions.explain: FDI can bring capital, technology and jobs, though with possible drawbacks.
